subject: [PATCH v4 0/2] iommu/arm-smmu-v3: Make the queue depths tunable, and shrink them in a kdump kernel

reviews.author: Nicolin Chen
reviews.summary:
Reviewer suggested minor cosmetic changes to the patch, indicating it looks cleaner after their review.

Reviewer Nicolin Chen suggested renaming module parameters for clarity, specifically recommending @ceiling and @ent_sz_shift instead of max_n_shift and cmdq_entries to better convey their purpose.

Reviewer Nicolin Chen suggested that the natural alignment cap should be moved to a more suitable location in the arm_smmu_cmdq_max_n_shift function, specifically after the ceiling is capped.

Reviewer suggested replacing IDR1 maxima-based calculation for cmdq.q.llq.max_n_shift with FIELD_GET() at the two call sites to simplify code

reviews.author: Nicolin Chen
reviews.summary: Reviewer Nicolin Chen suggested refactoring the code to use two small helpers for calculating event queue and priority queue maximum depths instead of a single function.

2026-09-06.patch_summary: This patch allows the queue depths of an ARM SMMU v3 device to be tuned, and reduces their size in a kdump kernel to conserve memory. The command queue depth is made tunable through a module parameter, while the event and priority queues are shrunk to one page by default in a kdump kernel. This change aims to reduce memory usage in a capture kernel without compromising system functionality.
